title: M17 scheduled-graph concurrent recovery repair
repair_summary: resume_graph_mission treats recovery_claimed and not_resumable:* as contention; converges when graph already SUCCEEDED; otherwise returns in_progress without settling a failed recovered mission
settle_recovered reloads peer terminal state / reports settle_in_progress instead of inventing a second failure
ScheduledGraphCoordinator.recover prefers an already-terminal recovered mission; on in_progress leaves occurrence recoverable instead of finishing OCC_FAILED from the original mission
settle_occurrence_from_mission reloads occurrence when finish_occurrence reports already_terminal
concurrency_scope_proven: in_process multi-thread callers sharing one RunLedger (sqlite BEGIN IMMEDIATE claims)
concurrency_scope_not_proven: multi-process multi-interpreter workers without additional evidence
limitations: Proven for in-process multi-thread concurrency on the sqlite RunLedger; multi-process/distributed safety is not certified here.
in_progress losers may require a subsequent recover() or reconcile pass to settle the occurrence; that is intentional and recoverable, not a silent success.
Adversarial coverage is the races encoded in tests and the stress harness, not a formal proof of all interleavings.
verdict_reasons: root cause identified and fixed at mission recovery + occurrence settlement layers without a parallel recovery subsystem
deterministic race tests and 175 stress iterations show zero duplicate graphs and zero contention-only false failures
critical-regressions and full local suite pass
clean-clone validation passes from tracked content
scope limitation remains for multi-process/distributed workers
